statement: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers or other mathematical objects with elements or entries arranged in rows and columns, denoted $\mathbf{A} = [a_{i,j}]$ where $1 \le i \le m$ denotes the row index and $1 \le j \le n$ denotes the column index for an $m \times n$ matrix.

symbols.meaning: entry or element of the matrix at the ith row and jth column

properties.property: Matrix subtraction is defined via scalar multiplication by -1: $\mathbf{A} - \mathbf{B} = \mathbf{A} + (-1) \cdot \mathbf{B}$
properties.why: subtraction is consistent with the composition of matrix addition and scalar multiplication

properties.property: The transpose $\mathbf{A}^{\mathrm{T}}$ of an $m \times n$ matrix $\mathbf{A}$ is the $n \times m$ matrix with $(\mathbf{A}^{\mathrm{T}})_{i,j} = \mathbf{A}_{j,i}$, satisfying $(c\mathbf{A})^{\mathrm{T}} = c(\mathbf{A}^{\mathrm{T}})$, $(\mathbf{A} + \mathbf{B})^{\mathrm{T}} = \mathbf{A}^{\mathrm{T}} + \mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{T}}$, and $(\mathbf{A}^{\mathrm{T}})^{\mathrm{T}} = \mathbf{A}$
properties.why: formed by turning rows into columns and vice versa

properties.property: Matrix multiplication $\mathbf{AB}$ of an $m \times n$ matrix $\mathbf{A}$ and an $n \times p$ matrix $\mathbf{B}$ produces an $m \times p$ matrix with entries $[\mathbf{AB}]_{i,j} = \sum_{r=1}^{n} a_{i,r} b_{r,j}$
properties.why: defined by the dot product of the corresponding row of $\mathbf{A}$ and column of $\mathbf{B}$, representing composition of linear transformations

properties.property: Matrix multiplication is associative $((\mathbf{AB})\mathbf{C} = \mathbf{A}(\mathbf{BC}))$ and distributive, but generally non-commutative $(\mathbf{AB} \neq \mathbf{BA})$
properties.why: corresponds to the composition of linear maps whose order of application matters

properties.property: A real $m \times n$ matrix $\mathbf{A}$ uniquely represents a linear transformation $f: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m$ via $\mathbf{x} \mapsto \mathbf{Ax}$
properties.why: the $(i, j)$-entry of $\mathbf{A}$ is the $i$th coordinate of $f(\mathbf{e}_j)$

properties.property: Multiplication with the identity matrix leaves a matrix unchanged: $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{I}_n = \mathbf{I}_m\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{A}$
properties.why: the identity matrix has ones on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere

assumptions.assumption: Matrix multiplication $\mathbf{AB}$ requires the number of columns of the left matrix $\mathbf{A}$ to equal the number of rows of the right matrix $\mathbf{B}$
assumptions.breaks_when: The column dimension of $\mathbf{A}$ is not equal to the row dimension of $\mathbf{B}$

assumptions.assumption: Matrix addition and subtraction require the operand matrices to have identical row and column dimensions
assumptions.breaks_when: Operands have mismatched row or column counts

failure_modes.cause: $\mathbf{A}$ has dimensions $m \times n$ and $\mathbf{B}$ has dimensions $k \times p$ with $n \ne k$
$\mathbf{A}$ is non-square or there exists no matrix $\mathbf{B}$ such that $\mathbf{AB} = \mathbf{BA} = \mathbf{I}_n$
